tsa-a03-v01.quick_english: When the light-formed Siva-tattva cannot enter the undivided mandala, seeing greater autonomy alone, he experiences non-conceptual Bhairava-immersion — this is his teaching: all this mass of states is a reflection in the sky of knowing, since what differs cannot stand alone and appears only by mixture with another; reflection is like a face in a mirror, taste in teeth-water, smell in nostrils, paired touch in the bliss-organ, spear-and-pitchfork touch in the inner organ, an echo in sky.

tsa-a03-v02.quick_english: For that flavor is not primary, since it acts by curing disease and the rest through an occult eye.

tsa-a03-v03.quick_english: Nor are smell and touch primary, being qualitied — in their absence, from impossibility, as the effect-chain begins.

tsa-a03-v04.quick_english: And they are not absent either: from seeing body-stripping, seed and the rest.

tsa-a03-v05.quick_english: Sound too is not primary: someone speaks it — heard like an echo of those coming.

tsa-a03-v06.quick_english: As what is reflected shines, so the world shines in the Supreme Lord's light.

tsa-a03-v07.quick_english: But what is the mirror-image here? Let it not be anything at all.

tsa-a03-v08.quick_english: How is that causeless? Then the reason-question: why? By the logic of mirror-speech — and the reason will be the Supreme Lord's power, synonym of autonomy; from world-reflection-bearing comes the Lord's world-selfhood, for consciousness-made is the world, the place of consciousness-manifestation; this world here is obstruction — reflection-bearing; but that world-selfhood is the Lord's own nature, not un-contradicted, since self-nature-contemplation of consciousness-nature is impossible.

tsa-a03-v09.quick_english: For in self-nature-contemplation there would in reality be inertness; and this contemplation does not depend on another but is inseparable from consciousness-nature merely — the womb of supreme sound, so said: he is exactly as much the Lord's world-establishing power-group as he contemplates.

tsa-a03-v10.quick_english: Three primary powers of the Supreme Lord: unsurpassable-will-awakening — that triad a i u; from this triad the whole power-manifold is carried. Unsurpassable is rest, bliss — rest in will is rulership — awakening is rest, wave: the beginning of action-power is that triad ā ī ū.

tsa-a03-v11.quick_english: Therein the prior triad is sun-natured, from being essence of the light-part; the final triad moon-natured, from prevalence of rest-nature-bliss — as far as the action-portion does not enter.

tsa-a03-v12.quick_english: When action enters will and rulership, it is called iṣyamāṇa-īśyamāṇa: two kinds — by mere light ra-utterance, by rest la-utterance; from being light-and-stopping nature. The willed is not distinct like the external — in distinct form would be its own creation; nor will or rulership — from non-distinctness, merely hearing, no standing like expression.

tsa-a03-v13.quick_english: This quad of letters is neuter, from bearing both shades: ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ.

tsa-a03-v14.quick_english: In the spread of unsurpassable-bliss in will and the rest, the pair e oṃ.

tsa-a03-v15.quick_english: Even further, from the union of unsurpassable bliss, the pair ai au.

tsa-a03-v16.quick_english: This is action-power — the quad e ai o au.

tsa-a03-v17.quick_english: Then in action-power-end all becomes effect as far as it will enter the unsurpassable; just so prior, standing as essence of consciousness, as mere light, as point — am.

tsa-a03-v18.quick_english: Then from it the seed-drop of the unsurpassable is born — aḥ.

tsa-a03-v19.quick_english: Thus the sixteenfold seed-form of contemplations is called.

tsa-a03-v21.quick_english: Therein from the unsurpassable the ka-class of faith-will, the ca-class of object-will, the double ṭa- and ta-class from awakening, the pa-class — from union with the five-power-group, fivefoldness.

tsa-a03-v22.quick_english: Of threefold will: ya ra lā from awakening, the va-letter; of threefold will: śa ṣa sā from visarga, the ha-letter, kṣa born of womb-union.

tsa-a03-v23.quick_english: Thus this Lord is the unsurpassable in form of the clan-Lord.

tsa-a03-v24.quick_english: His one kaulic seed-power, by which, from bliss-form onward, up to external creation, class-and-rest contemplations have attained tattva-form outside.

tsa-a03-v25.quick_english: That seed-drop is threefold: āṇava, form of mind-rest; śākta, marked by mind-awakening; śāṃbhava, form of mind-dissolution.

tsa-a03-v26.quick_english: Thus the seed-drop itself is the Lord's power in world-birth.

tsa-a03-v27.quick_english: When contemplation is by undividedness alone, then the Lord is one — by seed-womb, part-wise in contemplation, power-endowed and power.

tsa-a03-v28.quick_english: Separate in eightfold contemplation, in union with the wheel-Lord, nine-class; in prevalence of each single contemplation, fiftyfold.

tsa-a03-v29.quick_english: Even there, in contemplation of possible part-difference, eightyfold.

tsa-a03-v30.quick_english: In reality six contemplations; by spreading-and-returning twelve — they nourish the Supreme Lord's world-power fullness.

tsa-a03-v31.quick_english: Those very powers, from being contemplation-form, are the Lord's Śrīkālikā — so named.

tsa-a03-v32.quick_english: These too, power-formed pure contemplations, in pure-vidyā, by para-apara-form, from contraction of māyā-awakening merely, share vidyā-vidyeśvara-nature.

tsa-a03-v33.quick_english: In māyā again, crystal-formed difference-divisions assume māyic letter-nature — those who, having attained mundane-status in paśyantī-madhya-vaikharī, stand up to external form-tattva-nature; seen as body-like, revivified by pure contemplations the life-replacing, they become vigorous, granting enjoyment and liberation; thus, seeing self made merely of all-contemplation-rest, the reflection of all tattva-being-world-divisions, by non-conceptuality, by śāṃbhava-immersion, liberated-while-living.

tsa-a03-v34.quick_english: Even here, as before, no obstruction of mantra and the rest.

tsa-a03-v01.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v01.question: What is the upadeśa about the reflected world?
premises: śivatattvaṃ prakāśarūpam uktam — the light-formed Siva-tattva has been told.
akhaṇḍamaṇḍale praveṣṭuṃ na śaknoti — it cannot enter the undivided mandala.
svātantryaśaktiṃ paśyan nirvikalpaṃ bhairavasamāveśam anubhavati — seeing greater autonomy, non-conceptual Bhairava-immersion follows.
sarvaṃ bhāvajātaṃ bodhagagane pratibimbam — all states are reflection in the sky of knowing.
mukharūpam iva darpaṇe, rasa iva dantodake, pratiśrutkeva vyomni — face/taste/smell/touch/echo similes mark the reflection's dependence.
tsa-a03-v01.inference: The teaching (upadeśa) is that the world shows as pratibimba: what appears only by mixture with another cannot stand alone, so immersion is nirvikalpa, not world-entry.

tsa-a03-v02.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v02.question: Why is rasa not primary?
premises: na hi sa raso mukhyaḥ — taste is denied primacy.
tatkāryavyādhiśamanādyadṛṣṭeḥ — its works (disease-pacification and rest) run by an occult eye.
tsa-a03-v02.inference: Taste's efficacy depends on another sight, so it is kārya-effect, not mukhya-primary.

tsa-a03-v03.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v03.question: Why are gandha and sparśa not primary either?
premises: nāpi gandhasparśau mukhyau — smell and touch also denied primacy.
guṇinaḥ tatrābhāve — they are qualitied; in the absence of the qualitied they fail.
ayogāt, kāryaparamparānārambhāt ca — from impossibility and the effect-chain's beginning.
tsa-a03-v03.inference: Qualitied means dependent-on-substrate; dependence disqualifies primacy for both.

tsa-a03-v04.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v04.question: Yet smell and touch are not simply absent — what shows that?
premises: na ca tau na staḥ — the pair are not-nonexistent either.
dehoddhūlanavisargādidarśanāt — from seeing body-stripping, seed and rest.
tsa-a03-v04.inference: Somatic signs (uddhūlana, visarga) evidence their presence: denied as primary, not denied as existent.

tsa-a03-v05.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v05.question: Why is śabda not primary?
premises: śabdo 'pi na mukhyaḥ — sound too is denied primacy.
ko 'pi vakti iti — someone speaks it: sound requires a speaker.
āgacchantyā iva pratiśrutkāyāḥ śravaṇāt — heard like an echo of one arriving.
tsa-a03-v05.inference: Echo-hearing shows sound arrives from another: derivative, hence not mukhya.

tsa-a03-v06.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v06.question: What does the pratibimba claim extend to?
premises: yathā tat pratibimbitaṃ bhāti, tathaiva viśvaṃ parameśvaraprakāśe — as the reflection shines, so the world in the Lord's light.
tsa-a03-v06.inference: The mirror-model scales: viśva is pratibimba of parameśvara-prakāśa, nothing self-luminous below the Lord.

tsa-a03-v07.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v07.question: What could the bimba here be — is there a real image?
premises: nanu atra bimbaṃ kiṃ syāt — but what is the image here?
mābhūt kiṃcit — let there be no thing at all.
tsa-a03-v07.inference: The questioner's bimba is dissolved: reflection without a standing second entity — anuttara-model.

tsa-a03-v08.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v08.question: How is the world causeless-looking — what is the real hetu?
premises: nanu kim akāraṇakaṃ tat — how is that causeless?
hetuś ca parameśvaraśaktir eva svātantryāparaparyāyā — the reason is the Lord's power, synonym of autonomy.
viśvapratibimbadhāritvāc ca viśvātmakatvaṃ bhagavataḥ — world-reflection-bearing yields the Lord's world-selfhood.
saṃvinmayaṃ hi viśvaṃ caitanyasya vyaktisthānam — consciousness-made, the world is consciousness-manifestation-place.
citsvabhāvasya svarūpānāmarśanānupapatteḥ — self-nature-contemplation of consciousness-nature is impossible.
tsa-a03-v08.inference: Apparent causelessness resolves to svātantrya-śakti: the Lord bears the reflection, so viśvātmakatva is svarūpa, not an ascribed relation.

tsa-a03-v09.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v09.question: Does svarūpa-āmarśa reduce to jaḍatā — and what saves it?
premises: svarūpāmarśane vastuto jaḍataiva syāt — self-contemplation would be inertness in reality.
āmarśaś ca ayaṃ na sāketikaḥ — this contemplation depends-on-no-other.
api tu citsvabhāvatāmātranāntarīyakaḥ — inseparable from consciousness-nature merely.
paranādagarbha uktaḥ — womb of supreme sound, so called.
yāvān viśvavyavasthāpakaḥ parameśvaraśaktikalāpaḥ tāvantam āmṛśati — he contemplates exactly the Lord's world-establishing power-group.
tsa-a03-v09.inference: Āmarśa escapes jaḍatā by being citsvabhāva-identical: the contemplating measure equals the world-establishing śakti-measure.

tsa-a03-v10.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v10.question: What are the primary śaktis and their varṇa-triads?
premises: tisraḥ parameśvarasya śaktayaḥ anuttarecchonmeṣaḥ — three primary powers: unsurpassable will-awakening.
tat parāmarśatrayam a i u — that triad is a i u.
etasmād tritayāt sarvaḥ śaktiprapañcaḥ caryate — from this triad the whole power-manifold is carried.
anuttare viśrāntir ānandaḥ — in unsurpassable, rest is bliss; icchāyām īśanam — rest in will is rulership.
unmeṣe viśrāntir ūrmiḥ — awakening's rest is the wave; kriyāśakteḥ prārambhaḥ tat parāmarśatrayam ā ī ū — action-power's beginning is ā ī ū.
tsa-a03-v10.inference: The bīja-scheme is doctrinal: a i u = icchā-ānanda-īśana triad, ā ī ū = kriyā's commencement — sound encodes the power-structure.

tsa-a03-v11.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v11.question: How are the two triads characterized cosmically?
premises: prācyaṃ parāmarśatrayam prakāśabhāgasāratvāt sūryātmakam — the prior triad, essence-of-light-part, is sun-natured.
caramaṃ parāmarśatrayam viśrāntisvabhāvāhlādaprādhānyāt somātmakam — the final, rest-bliss-prevalent, moon-natured.
iyati yāvat karmāṃśasyānupraveśo nāsti — up to where the action-portion does not enter.
tsa-a03-v11.inference: Sun/moon marks the triads' function-boundary: light-side before action-entry, bliss-rest after.

tsa-a03-v12.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v12.question: When karma enters icchā-īśana, what results?
premises: yadā icchāyām īśane ca karma anupraviśati — when action enters will and rulership.
tat iṣyamāṇam īśyamāṇam iti ucyate — it is called iṣyamāṇa and īśyamāṇa.
dvau bhedau: prakāśamātreṇa raśrutiḥ, viśrāntyā laśrutiḥ — two kinds: ra by mere light, la by rest.
ralayoḥ prakāśastambhasvabhāvatvāt — ra and la are light-and-stopping natured.
asphuṭatvāt eva śrutimātraṃ ralayoḥ — from non-distinctness, only hearing stands, no expression.
tsa-a03-v12.inference: Action-in-will bifurcates into ra/la uttara-varṇas whose nature is prakāśa-stambha: heard-not-expressed, hence śruti-mātra.

tsa-a03-v13.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v13.question: Why is the ṛ-quad napuṃsaka?
premises: tat varṇacatuṣṭayam ubhayacchāyādhāritvāt napuṃsakam — the quad ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ is neuter.
ubhaya-chāyā-dhārita — it bears both shades (masculine/feminine).
tsa-a03-v13.inference: Neuter marks double-shade-bearing: the r-vowels sit between the gendered poles.

tsa-a03-v14.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v14.question: Which pair appears at the anuttara-ānanda spread?
premises: anuttarānandayoḥ icchādiṣu yadā prasaraḥ — when the spread of unsurpassable-bliss runs in will and rest.
tadā varṇadvayam e oṃ — the pair is e and oṃ.
tsa-a03-v14.inference: e/oṃ encode the anuttara-ānanda spread-point in the bīja sequence.

tsa-a03-v15.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v15.question: Which pair follows from anuttara-ānanda-saṃghaṭṭa?
premises: tatrāpi punar anuttarānandasaṃghaṭṭāt varṇadvayam ai au — from the union of unsurpassable bliss, ai au.
tsa-a03-v15.inference: ai/au mark the saṃghaṭṭa (union) moment — a further fold of the same spread.

tsa-a03-v16.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v16.question: What is kriyā-śakti in varṇa terms?
premises: sā iyaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ — this is action-power.
tad eva varṇacatuṣṭayam e ai o au — that very quad is e ai o au.
tsa-a03-v16.inference: The four diphthongs ARE kriyā-śakti: vowel-quad = action-power signature.

tsa-a03-v17.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v17.question: What stands at kriyāśaktyanta before anuttara-entry?
premises: kriyāśaktyante sarvaṃ kāryabhūtaṃ — at action-power's end all is effect.
yāvat anuttare pravekṣyati, tāvad eva pūrvaṃ saṃvedanasāratayā prakāśamātratvena bindutayā āste am — until entry, prior stands as consciousness-essence, mere light, point: am.
tsa-a03-v17.inference: am is the bindu-state: all-effect pending, standing as prakāśa-mātra at the threshold of anuttara.

tsa-a03-v18.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v18.question: What is born from that bindu?
premises: tatas tatraiva anuttarasya visargo jāyate aḥ — then the unsurpassable's visarga is born: aḥ.
tsa-a03-v18.inference: aḥ is anuttara's own visarga — the seed-drop born at the am-point.

tsa-a03-v19.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v19.question: What does this totalize to?
premises: evaṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ parāmarśānāṃ bījasvarūpam ucyate — thus the sixteenfold seed-form of contemplations.
tsa-a03-v19.inference: a + i u + ā ī ū + e oṃ + ai au + e ai o au + am + aḥ =16 bījas: parāmarśa's complete seed-scheme.

tsa-a03-v20.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v20.question: What kind of form arises from these seeds?
premises: tadutthaṃ vyañjanātmakaṃ yonirūpam — born-from-that, expression-natured, womb-form.
tsa-a03-v20.inference: The seed-scheme yields vyañjana-yoni: expressive womb from which the consonant-classes descend.

tsa-a03-v21.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v21.question: How do the consonant-classes distribute over the śaktis?
premises: anuttarāt kavargaḥ śraddhāyāḥ — from anuttara, ka-class of śraddhā (faith-will).
cavargaḥ sakarmikāyā icchāyāḥ — ca-class of object-bearing will.
dvau ṭavargas tavargaś ca unmeṣāt — double ṭa/ta-class from unmeṣa.
pavargaḥ śaktipañcakayogāt — pa-class from five-power union.
pañcakatvam — hence fivefoldness.
tsa-a03-v21.inference: Varga-distribution maps consonant-classes onto the śakti-structure: faith, object-will, awakening, fivefold-union.

tsa-a03-v22.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v22.question: What do ya/ra/lā, śa/ṣa/sā, kṣa encode?
premises: icchāyā eva trividhāyā ya ra lāḥ unmeṣāt — of threefold will, ya ra lā from unmeṣa.
vakāraḥ — the va-letter likewise.
icchāyā eva trividhāyāḥ śa ṣa sāḥ visargāt — of threefold will, śa ṣa sā from visarga.
hakāraḥ — the ha-letter likewise.
yonisaṃyogajaḥ kṣakāraḥ — kṣa born of yoni-union.
tsa-a03-v22.inference: Each letter-cluster carries its generation-ground: unmeṣa-lineage vs visarga-lineage, kṣa from yoni-conjunction.

tsa-a03-v23.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v23.question: What does the scheme identify the Lord as?
premises: ity eṣa bhagavān anuttara eva kuleśvararūpaḥ — thus the Lord is anuttara in kuleśvara-form.
tsa-a03-v23.inference: The bīja-analysis terminates in theology: the whole scheme is anuttara-as-kuleśvara.

tsa-a03-v24.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v24.question: How does kaulikī visarga-śakti produce the tattvas?
premises: tasya ekaiva kaulikī visargaśaktiḥ — his one kaulic visarga-power.
yayā ānandarūpāt prabhṛti bahiḥsṛṣṭiparyantena praspandataḥ — throbbing from bliss-form to outer-creation's end.
vargādiparāmarśā eva bahis tattvarūpatāṃ prāptāḥ — class-contemplations outward attain tattva-form.
tsa-a03-v24.inference: One kaulic visarga-throb externalizes the varga-parāmarśas into standing tattvas: emanation is visarga-driven.

tsa-a03-v25.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v25.question: How is that visarga threefold?
premises: sa visargas tridhā — the visarga is threefold.
āṇavaḥ cittaviśrāntirūpaḥ — āṇava: form of mind-rest.
śāktaḥ cittasaṃbodhalakṣaṇaḥ — śākta: marked by mind-awakening.
śāṃbhavaḥ cittapralayarūpaḥ — śāṃbhava: form of mind-dissolution.
tsa-a03-v25.inference: The three visarga-modes = the three consciousness-movements: sthiti, saṃbodha, pralaya.

tsa-a03-v26.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v26.question: What role does visarga play in world-birth?
premises: evaṃ visarga eva viśvajanane bhagavataḥ śaktiḥ — visarga is the Lord's power in world-birth.
tsa-a03-v26.inference: World-generation itself is visarga-operation: the seed-drop, not a separate creator-will.

tsa-a03-v27.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v27.question: What happens when parāmarśa is undivided?
premises: yadā nirvibhāgatayā eva parāmarśaḥ — when contemplation is by undividedness alone.
tadā eka eva bhagavān bījayonitayā — then the Lord is one, as seed-womb.
bhāgaśaḥ parāmarśe śaktimān śaktiś ca — part-wise in contemplation, power-endowed and power.
tsa-a03-v27.inference: Undivided = ekatva of Lord and śakti; divided = the śaktimān/śakti dyad — the bīja-yoni keeps both readings.

tsa-a03-v28.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v28.question: What do aṣṭaka and ekaika parāmarśas yield?
premises: pṛthak aṣṭakaparāmarśe cakreśvarasāhityena navavargaḥ — separate eightfold, with cakreśvara, nine-class.
ekaikaparāmarśaprādhānye pañcāśadātmakatā — in each-contemplation's prevalence, fiftyfold.
tsa-a03-v28.inference: Combinatorics of parāmarśa generate 9 and 50 class-counts: the scheme is generative, not merely classificatory.

tsa-a03-v29.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v29.question: What does possible part-difference contemplation yield?
premises: sambhavadbhāgabhedaparāmarśane ekāśītirūpatvam — in contemplation of possible part-difference, eightyfold.
tsa-a03-v29.inference: Allowing bheda within sambhavatā raises the count to 80 — numbers track doctrinal permissions.

tsa-a03-v30.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v30.question: What is the true count and what does it nourish?
premises: vastutas tu ṣaṭ eva parāmarśāḥ — in reality six contemplations.
prasaraṇapratisaṃcaraṇayogena dvādaśa — by spreading-and-returning, twelve.
parameśvarasya viśvaśaktipūrṇatvaṃ puṣṇanti — they nourish the Lord's world-power fullness.
tsa-a03-v30.inference: 6×2=12 is the operative total: the parāmarśas feed the fullness of viśva-śakti, not a larger metaphysics.

tsa-a03-v31.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v31.question: What are these powers called?
premises: tā eva etāḥ parāmarśarūpatvāt śaktayo bhagavatyaḥ — those powers, contemplation-formed, are the Lord's.
śrīkālikā iti niruktāḥ — Śrīkālikā they are named.
tsa-a03-v31.inference: Parāmarśa-as-śakti = Śrīkālikā: the technical term names the contemplating powers themselves.

tsa-a03-v32.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v32.question: How do pure parāmarśas relate to vidyā/vidyeśvara?
premises: ete śaktirūpā eva śuddhāḥ parāmarśāḥ — these pure contemplations are power-formed.
śuddhavidyāyāṃ parāpararūpatvena — in pure-vidyā by para-apara-form.
māyonmeṣamātrasaṃkocāt — from māyā-awakening's mere contraction.
vidyāvidyeśvararūpatāṃ bhajante — they share vidyā-vidyeśvara-nature.
tsa-a03-v32.inference: Purity-condition = para-apara-form in śuddha-vidyā; contraction of māyā-onmeṣa is what splits them into vidyā/vidyeśvara.

tsa-a03-v33.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v33.question: What happens to māyic divisions when re-quickened by pure parāmarśas?
premises: māyāyāṃ sphaṭībhūtabhedavibhāgā māyīyavarṇatāṃ bhajante — in māyā, crystal-formed divisions take māyic letter-nature.
paśyantīmadhyamāvaikharīṣu vyāvahārikatvam āsādya bahīrūpatattvasvabhāvatāpattiparyantāḥ — attaining mundane-status in the three vāk levels up to external-tattva-nature.
uktanayaiḥ śuddhaiḥ parāmarśaiḥ pratyujjīvanaṃ kriyate — revivified by those pure contemplations.
tadā te savīryā bhavanti, bhogamokṣapradāḥ — then vigorous, granting enjoyment and liberation.
sakalaparāmarśaviśrāntimātrarūpaṃ ātmānaṃ paśyato nirvikalpatayā śāṃbhavena samāveśena jīvanmuktatā — seeing self as all-contemplation-rest by śāṃbhava-immersion: liberated-while-living.
tsa-a03-v33.inference: Māyic varṇas revive under pure parāmarśa into bhoga-mokṣa-granters; the endpoint is jīvanmuktatā through nirvikalpa śāṃbhava-samāveśa.

tsa-a03-v34.speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
tsa-a03-v34.question: Does any mantra-obstruction remain at this level?
premises: atrāpi pūrvavat na mantrādiyantraṇā kācid — here too, as before, no obstruction of mantra and rest.
tsa-a03-v34.inference: The letter-scheme operates without mantra-yantraṇa: pure parāmarśa needs no ritual constraint, as before.

tsa-a03-v01.plain_english: The light-formed Siva-tattva has been told; but when it cannot enter the undivided mandala, seeing the greater power of autonomy alone, it experiences the non-conceptual immersion of Bhairava. This is his teaching: all this mass of states is a reflection in the sky of knowing — since reflection is marked by appearing in difference, unable to stand alone, shining only by mixture with another. The mark of reflection: a face in a mirror, taste in teeth-water, smell in nostrils, a paired touch in the bliss-organ, a spear-and-pitchfork touch in the inner touch-organ, an echo in the sky.
tsa-a03-v01.sanskrit_cite: yad etat prakāśarūpaṃ śivatattvam uktam tatra akhaṇḍamaṇḍale yadā praveṣṭuṃ na śaknoti tadā svātantryaśaktim eva adhikāṃ paśyan nirvikalpam eva bhairavasamāveśam anubhavati ayaṃ ca asya upadeśaḥ sarvam idaṃ bhāvajātaṃ bodhagagane pratibimbamātraṃ pratibimbalakṣaṇopetatvāt idaṃ hi pratibimbasya lakṣaṇaṃ yat bhedena bhāsitam aśaktam anyavyāmiśratvenaiva bhāti tat pratibimbam mukharūpam iva darpaṇe rasa iva dantodake gandha iva ghrāṇa mithunasparśa iva ānandendriye śūlakuntādisparśo vā antaḥsparśanendriye pratiśrutkeva vyomni

tsa-a03-v02.plain_english: That taste is not primary, because its works — curing disease and the rest — proceed by an occult eye.
tsa-a03-v02.sanskrit_cite: na hi sa raso mukhyaḥ tatkāryavyādhiśamanādyadṛṣṭeḥ

tsa-a03-v03.plain_english: Nor are smell and touch primary: they belong to qualities, and in the qualitied's absence they cannot be, since the effect-chain begins without them.
tsa-a03-v03.sanskrit_cite: nāpi gandhasparśau mukhyau guṇinaḥ tatra abhāve tayor ayogāt kāryaparamparānārambhāt ca

tsa-a03-v04.plain_english: And they are not simply nonexistent either — as body-stripping, seed, and the rest show.
tsa-a03-v04.sanskrit_cite: na ca tau na staḥ dehoddhūlanavisargādidarśanāt

tsa-a03-v05.plain_english: Sound too is not primary: someone speaks it, and it is heard like an echo of one arriving.
tsa-a03-v05.sanskrit_cite: śabdo 'pi na mukhyaḥ ko 'pi vakti iti āgacchantyā iva pratiśrutkāyāḥ śravaṇāt

tsa-a03-v06.plain_english: As that reflected thing shines, so the world shines in the light of the Supreme Lord.
tsa-a03-v06.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ yathā etat pratibimbitaṃ bhāti tathaiva viśvaṃ parameśvaraprakāśe

tsa-a03-v07.plain_english: But what would the image here be? Let it not be anything at all.
tsa-a03-v07.sanskrit_cite: nanu atra bimbaṃ kiṃ syāt mābhūt kiṃcit

tsa-a03-v08.plain_english: How is that causeless? Then comes the question of the reason: why? By the logic of mirror-speech the reason will be the Supreme Lord's power itself — the synonym of autonomy. And because it bears the world's reflection, the Lord's world-selfhood follows: consciousness-made is the world, the place where consciousness manifests — this world here is obstruction, reflection-bearing. But that world-selfhood is the Lord's own nature, not un-contradicted, since self-nature contemplation of consciousness-nature cannot be.
tsa-a03-v08.sanskrit_cite: nanu kim akāraṇakaṃ tat hanta tarhi hetupraśnaḥ tat kiṃ bimbavācoyuktyā hetuś ca parameśvaraśaktir eva svātantryāparaparyāyā bhaviṣyati viśvapratibimbadhāritvāc ca viśvātmakatvaṃ bhagavataḥ saṃvinmayaṃ hi viśvaṃ caitanyasya vyaktisthānam iti tad eva hi viśvam atra pratīpam iti pratibimbadhāritvam asya tac ca tāvat viśvātmakatvaṃ parameśvarasya svarūpaṃ na anāmṛṣṭaṃ bhavati citsvabhāvasya svarūpānāmarśanānupapatteḥ

tsa-a03-v09.plain_english: For in contemplation of the self's own nature there would in reality be mere inertness; and this contemplation does not depend on another — it is inseparable from consciousness-nature alone, the womb of supreme sound, so declared: as much as he is the Lord's world-establishing group of powers, so much does he contemplate.
tsa-a03-v09.sanskrit_cite: svarūpānāmarśane hi vastuto jaḍataiva syāt āmarśaś ca ayaṃ na sāketikaḥ api tu citsvabhāvatāmātranāntarīyakaḥ paranādagarbha uktaḥ sa ca yāvān viśvavyavasthāpakaḥ parameśvarasya śaktikalāpaḥ tāvantam āmṛśati

tsa-a03-v10.plain_english: There the three primary powers of the Supreme Lord are unsurpassable-will-awakening — that very triad is a i u. From this triad the whole play of powers is carried. In the unsurpassable, rest is bliss; rest in will is rulership; awakening's rest is the wave. The beginning of action-power is that triad ā ī ū.
tsa-a03-v10.sanskrit_cite: tatra mukhyās tāvat tisraḥ parameśvarasya śaktayaḥ anuttarecchonmeṣa iti tad eva parāmarśatrayam a i u iti etasmād eva tritayāt sarvaḥ śaktiprapañcaḥ caryate anuttara eva hi viśrāntir ānandaḥ icchāyām eva viśrāntiḥ īśanam unmeṣa eva hi viśrāntir ūrmiḥ yaḥ kriyāśakteḥ prārambhaḥ tad eva parāmarśatrayam ā ī ū iti

tsa-a03-v11.plain_english: There the prior triad of contemplations, being the essence of the light-part, is sun-natured; the final triad, by the prevalence of rest-natured bliss, is moon-natured — up to where the entry of the action-portion does not reach.
tsa-a03-v11.sanskrit_cite: atra ca prācyaṃ parāmarśatrayaṃ prakāśabhāgasāratvāt sūryātmakaṃ caramaṃ parāmarśatrayaṃ viśrāntisvabhāvāhlādaprādhānyāt somātmakam iyati yāvat karmāṃśasya anupraveśo nāsti

tsa-a03-v12.plain_english: When action enters will and rulership, what is entered and ruled is called iṣyamāṇa and īśyamāṇa. It has two kinds: by mere light, ra-utterance; by rest, la-utterance — ra and la being light-and-stopping in nature. And the willed is not distinct like the external — in distinctness would lie its own creation; nor is will or rulership distinct — from non-distinctness only hearing stands for ra and la, no stable expression.
tsa-a03-v12.sanskrit_cite: yadā tu icchāyām īśane ca karma anupraviśati yat tat iṣyamāṇam īśyamāṇam iti ca ucyate tadā asya dvau bhedau prakāśamātreṇa raśrutiḥ viśrāntyā laśrutiḥ ralayoḥ prakāśastambhasvabhāvatvāt iṣyamāṇaṃ ca na bāhyavat sphuṭam sphuṭarūpatve tad eva nirmāṇaṃ syāt na icchā īśanaṃ vā ataḥ asphuṭatvāt eva śrutimātraṃ ralayoḥ na vyañjanavat sthitiḥ

tsa-a03-v13.plain_english: This quad of letters is neuter, because it bears both shades: ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ.
tsa-a03-v13.sanskrit_cite: tad etad varṇacatuṣṭayam ubhayacchāyādhāritvāt napuṃsakam ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ iti

tsa-a03-v14.plain_english: When the spread of unsurpassable-bliss runs in will and the rest, the letter-pair is e and oṃ.
tsa-a03-v14.sanskrit_cite: anuttarānandayoḥ icchādiṣu yadā prasaraḥ tadā varṇadvayam e oṃ iti

tsa-a03-v15.plain_english: Further still, from the union of unsurpassable-bliss, the pair ai and au.
tsa-a03-v15.sanskrit_cite: tatrāpi punar anuttarānandasaṃghaṭṭāt varṇadvayam ai au iti

tsa-a03-v16.plain_english: This is action-power — and that very quad is e ai o au.
tsa-a03-v16.sanskrit_cite: sā iyaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ tad eva ca varṇacatuṣṭayam e ai o au iti

tsa-a03-v17.plain_english: Then at the end of action-power everything stands as effect; as far as it will enter the unsurpassable, just so long the prior stands as the essence of consciousness, as mere light, as the point: am.
tsa-a03-v17.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ punaḥ kriyāśaktyante sarvaṃ kāryabhūtaṃ yāvat anuttare pravekṣyati tāvad eva pūrvaṃ saṃvedanasāratayā prakāśamātratvena bindutayā āste am iti

tsa-a03-v18.plain_english: Then from that very place the visarga of the unsurpassable is born: aḥ.
tsa-a03-v18.sanskrit_cite: tatas tatraiva anuttarasya visargo jāyate aḥ iti

tsa-a03-v19.plain_english: Thus the sixteenfold seed-form of the contemplations is declared.

tsa-a03-v20.plain_english: Born from them, expression-natured, the womb-form.

tsa-a03-v21.plain_english: There from the unsurpassable comes the ka-class — of faith; the ca-class — of object-bearing will; the pair ṭa- and ta-classes — from awakening; the pa-class — from union with the five powers; hence fivefoldness.
tsa-a03-v21.sanskrit_cite: tatra anuttarāt kavargaḥ śraddhāyāḥ icchāyāḥ cavargaḥ sakarmikāyā icchāyā dvau ṭavargas tavargaś ca unmeṣāt pavargaḥ śaktipañcakayogāt pañcakatvam

tsa-a03-v22.plain_english: Of threefold will, ya ra lā come from awakening, and the va-letter; of threefold will, śa ṣa sā come from the visarga, and the ha-letter; the kṣa-letter is born of the womb-union.
tsa-a03-v22.sanskrit_cite: icchāyā eva trividhāyā ya ra lāḥ unmeṣāt vakāraḥ icchāyā eva trividhāyāḥ śa ṣa sāḥ visargāt hakāraḥ yonisaṃyogajaḥ kṣakāraḥ

tsa-a03-v23.plain_english: Thus this Lord is the unsurpassable himself, in the form of the clan-Lord.
tsa-a03-v23.sanskrit_cite: ity eva eṣa bhagavān anuttara eva kuleśvararūpaḥ

tsa-a03-v24.plain_english: His is one kaulic power of visarga, by which, from bliss-form onward to the end of outward creation, throbbing, the class-contemplations and the rest outward have attained the form of tattvas.
tsa-a03-v24.sanskrit_cite: tasya ca ekaiva kaulikī visargaśaktiḥ yayā ānandarūpāt prabhṛti iyatā bahiḥsṛṣṭiparyantena praspandataḥ vargādiparāmarśā eva bahis tattvarūpatāṃ prāptāḥ

tsa-a03-v25.plain_english: That visarga is threefold: āṇava, the form of mind's rest; śākta, marked by mind's awakening; śāṃbhava, the form of mind's dissolution.
tsa-a03-v25.sanskrit_cite: sa ca eṣa visargas tridhā āṇavaḥ cittaviśrāntirūpaḥ śāktaḥ cittasaṃbodhalakṣaṇaḥ śāṃbhavaḥ cittapralayarūpaḥ iti

tsa-a03-v26.plain_english: Thus the visarga itself is the Lord's power in the birth of the world.
tsa-a03-v26.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ visarga eva viśvajanane bhagavataḥ śaktiḥ

tsa-a03-v27.plain_english: When contemplation is by undividedness alone, then the Lord is one as the seed-womb — part-wise in contemplation, the power-endowed and the power.
tsa-a03-v27.sanskrit_cite: ity evam iyato yadā nirvibhāgatayā eva parāmarśaḥ tadā eka eva bhagavān bījayonitayā bhāgaśaḥ parāmarśe śaktimān śaktiś ca

tsa-a03-v28.plain_english: Separate in the eightfold contemplation, in union with the wheel-Lord, nine classes; in the prevalence of each single contemplation, fiftyfold.
tsa-a03-v28.sanskrit_cite: pṛthak aṣṭakaparāmarśe cakreśvarasāhityena navavargaḥ ekaikaparāmarśaprādhānye pañcāśadātmakatā

tsa-a03-v29.plain_english: Even there, in contemplation of a possibly differing part, eightyfold.

tsa-a03-v30.plain_english: In reality there are only six contemplations; by spreading and returning, twelve — they nourish the fullness of the Supreme Lord's world-power.
tsa-a03-v30.sanskrit_cite: vastutas tu ṣaṭ eva parāmarśāḥ prasaraṇapratisaṃcaraṇayogena dvādaśa bhavantaḥ parameśvarasya viśvaśaktipūrṇatvaṃ puṣṇanti

tsa-a03-v31.plain_english: Those very powers, being contemplation-formed, are the Lord's — Śrīkālikā they are named.
tsa-a03-v31.sanskrit_cite: tā eva etāḥ parāmarśarūpatvāt śaktayo bhagavatyaḥ śrīkālikā iti niruktāḥ

tsa-a03-v32.plain_english: These too, pure contemplations that are power-formed, in pure knowledge by the para-apara form, from the mere contraction of māyā's awakening, share the nature of the knower and the known.
tsa-a03-v32.sanskrit_cite: ete ca śaktirūpā eva śuddhāḥ parāmarśāḥ śuddhavidyāyāṃ parāpararūpatvena māyonmeṣamātrasaṃkocāt vidyāvidyeśvararūpatāṃ bhajante

tsa-a03-v33.plain_english: In māyā again, the crystal-clear divisions take māyic letter-nature — those who, attaining mundanity in paśyantī, madhyamā and vaikharī, stand up to the nature of external tattvas. When they are seen as body-like and revived by those pure contemplations — the life-replacing ones — they become vigorous, granting enjoyment and liberation. Thus, seeing oneself as merely the rest of all contemplations, as the reflection of all tattva-being-world divisions, by non-conceptuality, by the immersion of śāṃbhava — liberated while living.
tsa-a03-v33.sanskrit_cite: māyāyāṃ punaḥ sphaṭībhūtabhedavibhāgā māyīyavarṇatāṃ bhajante ye paśyantīmadhyamāvaikharīṣu vyāvahārikatvam āsādya bahīrūpatattvasvabhāvatāpattiparyantāḥ te ca māyīyā api śarīrakalpatvena yadā dṛśyante yadā ca teṣām uktanayair etaiḥ jīvitasthānīyaiḥ śuddhaiḥ parāmarśaiḥ pratyujjīvanaṃ kriyate tadā te savīryā bhavanti te ca tādṛśā bhogamokṣapradāḥ ity evaṃ sakalaparāmarśaviśrāntimātrarūpaṃ pratibimbitasamastatattvabhūtabhuvanabhedam ātmānaṃ paśyato nirvikalpatayā śāṃbhavena samāveśena jīvanmuktatā

tsa-a03-v34.plain_english: Even here, as before, there is no obstruction of mantra and the like.
tsa-a03-v34.sanskrit_cite: atrāpi pūrvavat na mantrādiyantraṇā kācid iti

essence: Light-formed Śiva-tattva cannot enter the undivided mandala — seeing autonomy, it falls into non-conceptual Bhairava-immersion; teaching: all states are reflection in knowing's sky.
Taste loses primacy: its works run through an occult eye.
Smell and touch lose primacy too: qualitied, they fail where the qualitied is absent — the effect-chain never starts from them.
Yet they are not nonexistent — body-stripping and seed attest their presence.
Sound loses primacy: a speaker is required, and it reaches us like an echo.
The world shines as reflection in the Supreme Lord's light, no self-luminosity below him.
The questioner's image is dissolved: let there be nothing at all standing there.
The apparent causelessness resolves into svātantrya-śakti — the Lord's power, synonym of autonomy, bears the world's reflection and so owns world-selfhood.
Self-nature contemplation would be inertness — saved from that only by being inseparable from consciousness-nature, the womb of supreme sound.
Three primary powers encode the bīja-triads: a i u for unsurpassable will-awakening, ā ī ū for action-power's onset.
Prior triad sun-natured by light-essence, final triad moon-natured by rest-bliss — the boundary where action-portion stops entering.
Action entering will and rulership births iṣyamāṇa/īśyamāṇa: ra by mere light, la by rest — heard, not expressed.
The r-quad is neuter because it carries both shades.
Surpassable-bliss spread in will yields the pair e oṃ.
The union of surpassable bliss adds ai au.
Action-power itself is the quad e ai o au.
At action-power's end all stands as effect — the prior standing as point, am, until unsurpassable entry.
From that point the unsurpassable's own visarga is born: aḥ.
The contemplation-seeds total sixteen — parāmarśa's bīja-form declared.
From those seeds rises the expression-natured womb-form.
Consonant-classes distribute over the powers: ka of faith, ca of object-will, double ṭa/ta of awakening, pa of fivefold union.
Letter-clusters carry generation-grounds — unmeṣa-lineage for ya-ra-lā, visarga-lineage for śa-ṣa-sā, yoni-born kṣa.
The whole scheme terminates in theology: anuttara as kuleśvara.
One kaulic visarga-throb externalizes the class-contemplations into tattva-forms.
The visarga is threefold as mind's rest, awakening, and dissolution — āṇava, śākta, śāṃbhava.
World-birth is visarga-operation itself — no separate creator-will needed.
Undivided contemplation collapses Lord and power into the one seed-womb; divided, the power-endowed/power dyad stands.
Eightfold yields nine classes with the wheel-Lord; each-contemplation-prevalence yields fifty.
Possible part-difference raises the count to eighty.
Reality holds six contemplations, twelve by spreading-and-returning — feeding the Lord's world-power fullness.
These contemplating powers are the Lord's — named Śrīkālikā.
Pure contemplations stand in pure knowledge as para-apara, contracting māyā's awakening into knower/known natures.
Māyic divisions revive under pure contemplations into vigors granting both enjoyment and liberation — the view ends in liberated-while-living.
Even here, as before, mantra and the like impose no obstruction.

rasa.dominant: śānta with vimarśa weight (rest carrying the letter-scheme)
rasa.sthayibhava: viśrānti (rest as the ground the bījas stand in)
rasa.justification: The relish is ordered disclosure: each refutation settles, each seed names, each count lands — and the chapter's own doctrine says rest is bliss, so its calm is content, not mood; the jīvanmuktatā close is the single rising chord.

Māyic divisions revive under pure contemplations into vigors granting both enjoyment and liberation — the view ends in liberated-while-living. Even here, as before, mantra and the like impose no obstruction.
sections.FUNCTION: Maps the parāmarśa-śakti doctrine: why the reflected world is not primary, the sixteen bīja-seeds of contemplation, the consonant-classes distributed over the powers, the threefold visarga, and the counts (9/50/80/6/12) that nourish the Lord's world-power — closing with Śrīkālikā, māyic revival, and jīvanmuktatā.
sections.KEY TERMS: pratibimba (reflection in bodha-gagana); svātantrya-śakti (autonomy-power as the real hetu); parāmarśa (contemplation as the bīja-substance); ṣoḍaśaka-bīja (the sixteen seeds a…aḥ); varga-distribution (consonant-classes over śaktis); visarga-tridhā (āṇava/śākta/śāṃbhava); Śrīkālikā (the contemplating powers' name); jīvanmuktatā (the śāṃbhava-samāveśa close).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Āhnika 3 follows the pratibimba opening of the ahnika-series and turns cosmology into phonology; the ra/la and bīja scheme feeds nothing later in Tantrasāra — a self-contained doctrine of letter-and-power; a14's rite-manual is the practical opposite face of this theory.
sections.BOUNDARY: Reflection doctrine argued by simile-chain, not by exclusion of other models; the counts (16/9/50/80/6/12) asserted without derivation shown; māyic revival stated as fact with no conditions given; mantra-freedom (u34) declared by appeal to 'as before' without restating the prior ground.
sections.EXPLANATION: The chapter moves: refutation of primaries (rasa/gandha/sparśa/śabda all derivative) → the reflection-model scaled to viśva → svātantrya-śakti as the real reason → the bīja-scheme (a i u … aḥ = sixteen) → consonant-classes mapped to powers → visarga as world-birth engine → combinatorial counts → Śrīkālikā → pure/māyic parāmarśas → revivification and the jīvanmuktatā close. Sound is doctrine here: every letter names a power-state.

lines: Then from that very place
the unsurpassable's visarga is born: aḥ.
tsa-a03-v18.sanskrit_cite: tatas tatraiva anuttarasya visargo jāyate aḥ iti

lines: So the contemplations' seed-form
stands sixteenfold.
Born from them, expression-natured,
the womb-form.
There from the unsurpassable: the ka-class
of faith; the ca-class of object-bearing will;
the pair ṭa- and ta-classes from awakening;
the pa-class from union with the five powers —
hence fivefold.
tsa-a03-v21.sanskrit_cite: tatra anuttarāt kavargaḥ śraddhāyāḥ icchāyāḥ cavargaḥ sakarmikāyā icchāyā dvau ṭavargas tavargaś ca unmeṣāt pavargaḥ śaktipañcakayogāt pañcakatvam

lines: Of threefold will: ya ra lā from awakening,
with the va-letter; śa ṣa sā from the visarga,
with the ha-letter; kṣa, born of the womb-union.
tsa-a03-v22.sanskrit_cite: icchāyā eva trividhāyā ya ra lāḥ unmeṣāt vakāraḥ icchāyā eva trividhāyāḥ śa ṣa sāḥ visargāt hakāraḥ yonisaṃyogajaḥ kṣakāraḥ

lines: Thus this Lord is the unsurpassable himself —
in the form of the clan-Lord.
tsa-a03-v23.sanskrit_cite: ity eva eṣa bhagavān anuttara eva kuleśvararūpaḥ

lines: His is one kaulic visarga-power, by which,
from bliss-form to the end of outward creation,
throbbing, the class-contemplations and the rest
outward have attained the form of tattvas.
tsa-a03-v24.sanskrit_cite: tasya ca ekaiva kaulikī visargaśaktiḥ yayā ānandarūpāt prabhṛti iyatā bahiḥsṛṣṭiparyantena praspandataḥ vargādiparāmarśā eva bahis tattvarūpatāṃ prāptāḥ

lines: That visarga is threefold: āṇava —
mind's rest; śākta — mind's awakening;
śāṃbhava — mind's dissolution.
tsa-a03-v25.sanskrit_cite: sa ca eṣa visargas tridhā āṇavaḥ cittaviśrāntirūpaḥ śāktaḥ cittasaṃbodhalakṣaṇaḥ śāṃbhavaḥ cittapralayarūpaḥ iti

lines: So the visarga itself is the Lord's power
for world-birth.
tsa-a03-v26.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ visarga eva viśvajanane bhagavataḥ śaktiḥ

lines: When contemplation is by undividedness alone,
the Lord is one as the seed-womb — divided in part,
the power-endowed and the power.
tsa-a03-v27.sanskrit_cite: ity evam iyato yadā nirvibhāgatayā eva parāmarśaḥ tadā eka eva bhagavān bījayonitayā bhāgaśaḥ parāmarśe śaktimān śaktiś ca

lines: Separate in the eightfold contemplation,
with the wheel-Lord: nine classes; in each
single contemplation's prevalence: fifty.
tsa-a03-v28.sanskrit_cite: pṛthak aṣṭakaparāmarśe cakreśvarasāhityena navavargaḥ ekaikaparāmarśaprādhānye pañcāśadātmakatā

lines: Even there, in contemplation of a possibly
differing part: eighty.
In reality six contemplations only;
by spreading and returning, twelve — they nourish
the fullness of the Lord's world-power.
tsa-a03-v30.sanskrit_cite: vastutas tu ṣaṭ eva parāmarśāḥ prasaraṇapratisaṃcaraṇayogena dvādaśa bhavantaḥ parameśvarasya viśvaśaktipūrṇatvaṃ puṣṇanti

lines: Those very powers, contemplation-formed,
are the Lord's — Śrīkālikā they are named.
tsa-a03-v31.sanskrit_cite: tā eva etāḥ parāmarśarūpatvāt śaktayo bhagavatyaḥ śrīkālikā iti niruktāḥ

lines: These too, pure contemplations, power-formed,
stand in pure knowledge as para-apara — from the mere
contraction of māyā's awakening, sharing the nature
of knower and known.
tsa-a03-v32.sanskrit_cite: ete ca śaktirūpā eva śuddhāḥ parāmarśāḥ śuddhavidyāyāṃ parāpararūpatvena māyonmeṣamātrasaṃkocāt vidyāvidyeśvararūpatāṃ bhajante

lines: In māyā again the crystal-clear divisions
take māyic letter-nature — those who, attaining
mundanity in paśyantī, madhyamā, vaikharī, stand up
to the nature of external tattvas. Seen body-like,
revived by those pure contemplations — the life-replacing —
they turn vigorous, granting enjoyment and liberation. Thus,
seeing oneself as the rest of all contemplation, as the
reflection of all tattva-being-world divisions —
non-conceptual, by śāṃbhava-immersion —
liberated while living.

lines: Even here, as before, no obstruction
of mantra and the like.
